mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary easing, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns over 20 days are not significantly positive despite a decline in FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Rising quarterly GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic demand, driving up corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns over 20 days are not significantly positive despite rising GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained low unemployment (UNRATE below 4%) reflects strong labor market confidence, fostering economic growth and positive equity returns, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns over 20 days are not significantly positive despite UNRATE remaining below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) and upward momentum in GDP (GDPC1) create a synergistic effect, amplifying S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < previous month AND GDPC1 > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns over 20 days are not significantly positive despite both FEDFUNDS declining and GDPC1 rising.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE below 4%) combined with rising GDP (GDPC1) signals robust economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns over 20 days are not significantly positive despite UNRATE below 4% and GDPC1 rising.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) signals reduced policy tightening pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns over 60 days are not significantly positive despite FEDFUNDS declining.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, rising industrial production (INDPRO) and declining federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) create a positive feedback loop, driving S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month AND FEDFUNDS < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns over 60 days are not significantly positive despite INDPRO rising and FEDFUNDS declining.

mechanism_narrative: A crossing of the federal funds rate above 5% triggers expectations of tighter monetary policy, reducing growth prospects and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns over 5 days are not significantly negative despite FEDFUNDS crossing above 5%.
